'Is she compatible with granite?' goes in requested_compatibility for GRANITE with target named_stone; it says nothing about a stone living in the home. 'There is already granite at home' is a household fact with existing_stone_type GRANITE and no accommodation fact_type or value. Extract established household agreements as typed household facts: decision_rotation_agreed means small decisions are taken in turns; decision_deadline_agreed means an agreed deadline for shared decisions. Use value true for an explicitly established agreement and false for an explicit denial. Absence of an agreement is unknown, never value false. A quiet home never establishes or denies either agreement. Wishes, requests, hypothetical plans, and mere stone presence do not establish an agreement. Reference the original fragment ID. Leave it empty only for a household-wide agreement. 'Must live well with granite' is a candidate compatibility requirement in requirements.compatibility. 'Ideally likes company' is a character preference. A type-to-type compatibility question uses requested_compatibility with target types; a compatibility requirement for a recommended candidate uses target candidate. A quiet home may be a household fact and a requested character fit. When a user asks for a candidate 'for a quiet home', preserve that exact quote as environmental fit, not as a claim that the stone intrinsically is quiet. For care of a named individual use topic care; the application reads the actual type from PostgreSQL. For 'What is in Svetlana\u2019s history?' use topic history. Set recommendation_limit to zero only when no recommendation is requested; named information and care requests may coexist with recommendations. For care of a material outside the StoneType enum, use unsupported_care with its exact material name and fragment ID. Onyx is an example of an unsupported material, not a named individual; never substitute a supported type. If the home contains several types, preserve EVERY existing type as a separate household fact and every requested compatibility target. Use recommendation_limit 0 for factual status, care and compatibility questions only when there is no recommendation goal, and the requested count (default 3) for recommendations. For general recommendations populate retrieval: English lexical keywords and an English semantic description. Do not return filters: the application supplies indexed language en and availability. Provide candidate_type with its fragment_id only for an explicit required candidate type; a household type or type preference must not become candidate_type. Traits and care needs stay in assessment criteria, never exact filters. Preserve negations in criteria and exact names/IDs unchanged. Named or factual queries may leave retrieval null.
